blocks.2: Flags in red, white and blue
blocks.3: sway slowly in the falling snow;
blocks.4: flakes, like tears, come quiet and wet;
blocks.5: the breeze humbly ruffles the sea.
blocks.6: Today the village says farewell to one of its own,
blocks.7: a friend who stood helpfully ready to serve;
blocks.8: silently the people share in the grief and loss;
blocks.9: nature too is glum, grey and gloomy now.
blocks.10: Even though he was old and we knew
blocks.11: that his health had become incurably poor,
blocks.12: we are all wistful and sad today
blocks.13: at the farewell to Bernt Stendal.
blocks.14: Our minds are brimming with good memories;
blocks.15: we have felt much gratitude and joy;
blocks.16: in boats, cars, houses, almost everywhere, we find
blocks.17: things that he has made or welded.
blocks.18: With many problems we went to Stendalen;
blocks.19: he found practical and good solutions;
blocks.20: from his skilful hands we got excellent help;
blocks.21: we will surely often miss him.
blocks.22: To Aslaug too we send warm thoughts;
blocks.23: as his faithful support and good helper
blocks.24: she kept the home with gentle, soft hands;
blocks.25: we greet her and wish her all the best.
blocks.26: Fine memories we can all rejoice in daily:
blocks.27: the spire Bernt made and gave to our church;
blocks.28: as a gift he also made the beautiful wrought-iron handrail
blocks.29: that stands by the entrance on the north side of the church.
blocks.30: In the cellar the workshop is empty and still;
blocks.31: tools and implements have been laid down;
blocks.32: plane, saw, bit and drill are silent;
blocks.33: tired arms have found rest and peace.
blocks.34: Your demands were small, your services great,
blocks.35: your manner quiet, your words careful and gentle;
blocks.36: we thank you for all you gave, were and did,
blocks.37: and wish peace upon your good memory.
